chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The toiler upon his family is like the combatant in the Way of Allah.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for working to support one's family in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the provision for one's family as a highly meritorious act of worship comparable to jihad. This hadith elevates the mundane duty of earning a halal livelihood to the spiritual status of striving in the path of Allah, emphasizing that familial responsibility is a primary form of ibadah. It underscores the Shia scholarly view that social and economic stability within the family unit is a fundamental religious obligation with significant eschatological rewards.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The toiler upon his family is like the combatant in the Way of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from af-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
A person working hard for his family is like Mujahid (fighter) for the cause of Allah. ’”
